subsystems.name: Scoop field generator
subsystems.role: creates the magnetic funnel, hundreds to thousands of kilometres across, that gathers interstellar gas.

subsystems.name: Pre-ionisation system
subsystems.role: neutral hydrogen ignores magnetic fields, so it must first be stripped of electrons.

subsystems.name: Collector and compressor
subsystems.role: funnels the captured plasma into a dense, hot core.

subsystems.name: Fusion core
subsystems.role: burns the collected hydrogen, releasing energy that drives the ship.

subsystems.name: Nozzle and energy conversion
subsystems.role: expels fusion products as thrust and, in some designs, recovers electricity.

subsystems.name: Vehicle
subsystems.role: carries the coils, reactor and payload at the lowest possible mass.

buildSteps.title: Fix the speed floor
buildSteps.detail: Because scooping gas also creates drag, the ship must already be moving fast for thrust to exceed drag. Mission studies would first define that minimum cruise speed — in published analyses a few percent of light speed or more.

buildSteps.title: Size the scoop field
buildSteps.detail: Coil radius, field strength and mass trade against each other: a larger field captures more gas but adds structure and drag. The target is the largest field a buildable coil array can sustain.

buildSteps.title: Validate capture in a vacuum chamber
buildSteps.detail: A scaled experiment fires a plasma stream past a magnet at interstellar-like densities (roughly 10^5–10^6 atoms per cubic metre) and measures what fraction is captured, and how much drag that costs.

buildSteps.title: Prove the ionisation stage
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate that the ioniser converts enough of the incoming neutral hydrogen to charged particles before it crosses the field, without wasting more energy than the fusion core returns.

buildSteps.title: Build the compressor and heater
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the magnetic funnel that squeezes collected plasma into the core and the radio-frequency or beam heating that brings it to fusion temperature.

buildSteps.title: Settle the fuel cycle
buildSteps.detail: Pure hydrogen fusion through the proton–proton chain is far too slow at achievable energies, so the design must either carry a catalyst for the CNO cycle or seed the plasma with a more reactive isotope — both are unresolved and carry their own mass penalty.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the core, nozzle and radiators
buildSteps.detail: Couple the reactor to a magnetic nozzle and to radiators big enough to reject unavoidable waste heat, then run the whole assembly in a ground test stand.

buildSteps.title: Pre-accelerate to operating speed
buildSteps.detail: A ramjet cannot start from rest with useful thrust, so it would be launched by beamed energy (as in laser-sail concepts) or staged fusion drives until it passes the speed floor.

buildSteps.title: Fly progressively
buildSteps.detail: Subscale robotic tests inside the solar system, then a fast interstellar probe, would come before any crewed ramjet.

prerequisites.why: no magnetic fusion device has yet produced more energy than it consumes, and a ramjet needs a lightweight one.
high-temperature superconducting magnets exist at metre scale, but nothing close to a field kilometres across has been built or flown.

prerequisites.tech: Validated magnetic scoop with net thrust
prerequisites.why: whether a scoop can capture more momentum as thrust than it loses as drag has never been shown experimentally.
the incoming gas is extremely thin, so the ioniser and heater must add far less energy than the core recovers.

prerequisites.tech: Beamed-energy or staged pre-acceleration to a few percent of light speed
prerequisites.why: laser-sail proposals such as Breakthrough Starshot (announced 2016) aim at roughly 0.2c for gram-scale payloads, but nothing of ramjet mass has been accelerated.

pathway.milestone: theory and computation: Bussard proposed the concept in 1960; later analyses showed scoop drag dominates at low speed and that the proton–proton reaction is far too slow without a catalyst
pathway.unlocks: a clear statement of the physics problems that must be solved before any hardware is worth building.

pathway.milestone: laboratory plasma experiments measuring magnetic scoop capture fraction and drag at interstellar-like densities
pathway.unlocks: an honest answer to whether net thrust is possible at all.

pathway.milestone: in-space tests of large-field plasma interaction, such as magnetic sails or plasma brakes flown from small spacecraft
pathway.unlocks: flight data on how a spacecraft-scale magnetic field behaves in a real, thin plasma.

pathway.milestone: a fusion drive that carries its own fuel (direct fusion drive), launched by beamed energy or staged boosters
pathway.unlocks: fast solar-system travel and the pre-acceleration a ramjet would need before its scoop becomes useful.

pathway.milestone: a ramjet that gathers its fuel in flight, once compact fusion, large coils and scoop physics all mature together
pathway.unlocks: interstellar cruise without carrying fuel mass — the original attraction of the idea.
